# AUDIT REPORT — CHUNK 4: UI / Bots / SEO

## FINDINGS

---

### 1. XSS via `|safe` on user-influenced weekly text
**[SEV: critical — P0]**
**File:** `app/templates/account.html:~68`

```html
<p style="margin:0; line-height:1.8; font-size:.92rem;">{{ w.text|safe }}</p>
```

**Evidence:** `w.text` comes from `weekly` dict values. If the weekly reflection text is generated by LLM or stored from any user-adjacent input, `|safe` renders raw HTML/JS in the user's browser. An LLM hallucinating `<script>` tags or a prompt-injection attack could achieve stored XSS.

**Fix:** Remove `|safe` and use auto-escaping: `{{ w.text }}`. If rich formatting is needed, sanitize server-side with `bleach` (allow only `<b>`, `<em>`, `<br>`) before passing to template.

---

### 2. XSS via `|safe` on `banner_svg` in article template
**[SEV: major — P1]**
**File:** `app/templates/article.html:10`

```html
<div class="article-banner" ...>{{ banner_svg | safe }}</div>
```

**Evidence:** If `banner_svg` is generated from article metadata or CMS content that an admin edits, this is an SVG injection vector. SVGs can contain `<script>`, `onload`, and `<foreignObject>` with arbitrary HTML. Even admin-only CMS content should be sanitized because admin account compromise → stored XSS for all visitors.

**Fix:** Sanitize SVG server-side (strip `<script>`, event handlers, `<foreignObject>`) before rendering, or serve SVGs as `<img src="...">` which sandboxes script execution.

---

### 3. Admin CMS: DOM-based XSS via unsanitized article data in `innerHTML`
**[SEV: critical — P0]**
**File:** `app/templates/admin.html:~95-120` (multiple `cmsList`, `cmsPages`, `cmsPageEdit` functions)

```javascript
h += `<tr ...><td>${a.title}</td><td dir="ltr">${a.slug}</td>...`;
// and
h += `<tr ...><td dir="ltr">${pg.key}</td><td>${pg.title}</td>...`;
```

**Evidence:** Article titles, slugs, page keys, and page titles are interpolated directly into HTML strings assigned to `innerHTML`. If any of these contain `<img onerror=alert(1)>` or similar, it executes. Even though this is an admin page, it's a self-XSS / privilege-escalation vector (one admin can attack another, or a compromised API response can attack the admin).

**Fix:** Use `textContent` for data cells, or escape HTML entities before interpolation:
```javascript
function esc(s) { const d = document.createElement('div'); d.textContent = s; return d.innerHTML; }
// then: h += `<td>${esc(a.title)}</td>`;
```

### 4. Admin withdrawal forms missing CSRF token
**[SEV: major — P1]**
**File:** `app/templates/admin.html:~410-420`

```html
<form method="post" action="/api/admin/withdrawals/{{ w.id }}/resolve" style="display:inline;margin-left:6px;">
  <input type="hidden" name="status" value="paid">
  <button class="btn" ...>تأیید واریز</button>
</form>
```

**Evidence:** Unlike the account delete form which includes `<input type="hidden" name="csrf_token" value="{{ csrf_token }}">`, these withdrawal resolution forms have no CSRF token. An attacker could craft a page that auto-submits this form, approving a fraudulent withdrawal.

**Fix:** Add `<input type="hidden" name="csrf_token" value="{{ csrf_token }}">` to both withdrawal forms (approve and reject).

### 5. Admin login: no CSRF protection on PIN form
**[SEV: moderate — P2]**
**File:** `app/templates/admin_login.html:10`

```html
<form method="post" action="/admin/login">
  <input name="pin" type="password" ...>
```

**Evidence:** No CSRF token. While the form only accepts a PIN, a CSRF attack could be used for login-CSRF (forcing an admin to log in as the attacker's admin account to capture subsequent actions). Lower severity because it requires knowing a valid PIN, but still a gap.

**Fix:** Add CSRF token to the admin login form.

### 6. Notification prefs save: no CSRF token sent
**[SEV: moderate — P2]**
**File:** `app/templates/account.html` (JS `notifPrefs.save()`)

```javascript
const r = await fetch('/api/notifications/prefs', { method: 'POST', body });
```

**Evidence:** The POST uses `URLSearchParams` but sends no CSRF token. If the API endpoint relies on cookie-based auth, this is CSRF-vulnerable. Same issue applies to `wallet.askWithdraw()`, `subs.doCancel()`, and the push subscribe flow — none send CSRF tokens.

**Fix:** Include CSRF token in all state-changing fetch calls. Either read from a meta tag or cookie:
```javascript
headers: { 'X-CSRF-Token': document.querySelector('meta[name=csrf-token]').content }
```

### 7. `prompt()` and `alert()` used in admin and wallet — poor mobile UX
**[SEV: moderate — P2]**
**File:** `app/templates/account.html` (wallet `askWithdraw`), `app/templates/admin.html` (multiple `alert()` calls, one `confirm()` in `cmsDel`)

```javascript
const v = prompt('مبلغ تسویه به ریال ...');
// ...
alert(r.ok ? 'درخواست تسویه ثبت شد ✅ ...' : ...);
```

```javascript
if (!confirm('حذف مقاله؟ ...')) return;
```

**Evidence:** The codebase explicitly notes (F-29 comment) that `confirm()` is "invisible/unreliable on mobile and banned by design rules." Yet `prompt()` is used for wallet withdrawal, `confirm()` for CMS article deletion, and `alert()` throughout admin. These are inconsistent with the stated design rules.

**Fix:** Replace `prompt()` with an inline Alpine modal with an input field. Replace remaining `confirm()` with the two-step pattern already used elsewhere. Replace `alert()` with inline toast/status messages.

### 8. Dev OTP code exposed in production login template
**[SEV: major — P1]**
**File:** `app/templates/account_login.html:22`

```html
<p class="muted" ... x-show="devCode">کد تست (dev): <b x-text="devCode" style="color:#f5c518;"></b></p>
```

**Evidence:** The login JS stores `this.devCode = d.dev_code || ''` from the API response. If the backend ever returns `dev_code` in production (even accidentally), the OTP is displayed in the UI. This is an authentication bypass risk.

**Fix:** Remove the `devCode` display entirely from the template. If needed for development, gate it behind a build-time flag that strips it from production HTML. The backend should never return `dev_code` in production, but defense-in-depth requires the frontend not to render it either.

### 11. `font-display: optional` may cause FOIT on slow connections
**[SEV: moderate — P2]**
**File:** `app/templates/base.html` (CSS `@font-face` declarations)

```css
font-display:optional;
```

**Evidence:** `font-display: optional` means the font is only used if it's already cached. On first visit over slow connections (common in Iran), users see the entire page in fallback font (Tahoma), which may render Persian text poorly. `swap` is generally preferred for RTL/Persian text to ensure the custom font loads.

**Fix:** Change to `font-display: swap` for at least the Regular and Bold weights.

### 12. Chart page: `access_token` leaked in Telegram share URL
**[SEV: major — P1]**
**File:** `app/templates/chart.html:~148`

```javascript
share(){
  const url = location.origin + '/chart/{{ chart.id }}?t={{ access_token }}';
  window.open('https://t.me/share/url?url=' + encodeURIComponent(url) + ...);
}
```

**Evidence:** The access token is embedded in the shared URL. Anyone who receives this Telegram message gets full access to the chart (and potentially report PDF download). The token is also visible in Telegram message previews, chat history, and link previews. If the token grants write access or is long-lived, this is a significant authorization leak.

**Fix:** Generate a separate, read-only, time-limited share token specifically for sharing. Don't reuse the session/access token.

### 13. Chart page: `{{ chart.id }}` and `{{ access_token }}` in inline JS without escaping
**[SEV: moderate — P2]**
**File:** `app/templates/chart.html` (multiple locations in `<script>`)

```javascript
const p = await fetch('/api/charts/{{ chart.id }}/preview?t={{ access_token }}');
```

**Evidence:** If `chart.id` or `access_token` contain characters like `'`, `</script>`, or `\`, they could break out of the JS context. UUIDs are typically safe, but this is a defense-in-depth concern. Jinja2's auto-escaping is for HTML context, not JS string context.

**Fix:** Use `{{ chart.id | tojson }}` and `{{ access_token | tojson }}` to ensure proper JS escaping.

### 14. `search_items|tojson` rendered without `|safe` — potential double-escaping
**[SEV: minor — P2]**
**File:** `app/templates/account.html` (JS `dashSearch`)

```javascript
items: {{ search_items|tojson }},
```

**Evidence:** In Jinja2 with auto-escaping enabled, `|tojson` output gets HTML-escaped (e.g., `"` → `&quot;`), breaking the JavaScript. This should use `{{ search_items|tojson|safe }}` — but then you must ensure `search_items` values are sanitized server-side to prevent XSS.

**Fix:** Use `{{ search_items|tojson }}` — in modern Flask/Jinja2 (3.x), `tojson` is already marked safe. Verify your Jinja2 version. If using older version, use `|safe` but sanitize input server-side.

### 15. Explore page: `cards_json`, `charts_json`, `active_chart_json` rendered with `|safe`
**[SEV: moderate — P2]**
**File:** `app/templates/explore.html:~120-122`

```javascript
cards: {{ cards_json|safe }},
charts: {{ charts_json|safe }},
chartId: {{ active_chart_json|safe }},
```

**Evidence:** If any card title, chart label, or other field contains user-controlled text (e.g., profile name), `|safe` in a `<script>` block enables XSS. An attacker could set their profile name to `</script><script>alert(1)</script>` and trigger execution.

**Fix:** Ensure all values in these JSON objects are sanitized server-side. Better: use `|tojson` (which handles JS-safe encoding) instead of pre-serializing and using `|safe`.

### 16. Articles index: Alpine category filter injection
**[SEV: moderate — P2]**
**File:** `app/templates/articles_index.html:12-14`

```html
<button ... @click="cat='{{ c }}'">{{ c }}</button>
...
x-show="cat==='همه' || cat==='{{ a.category }}'"
```

**Evidence:** Category names from CMS are interpolated directly into Alpine JS expressions. If a category name contains `'` (e.g., `it's`), it breaks the JS and could enable attribute injection. The trailing `'` in `{{ a.category }}'"` also looks like a syntax error (extra quote).

**Fix:** Use `{{ c|tojson }}` for JS context interpolation. Fix the trailing quote:
```html
x-show="cat==='همه' || cat==={{ a.category|tojson }}"
```

### 18. Missing `rel="noopener noreferrer"` on some external links
**[SEV: minor — P2]**
**File:** `app/templates/base.html` (analytics script), `app/templates/contact.html:13`

```html
<a ... href="https://t.me/Astrology_chartx_bot" target="_blank" rel="noopener">
```

**Evidence:** `rel="noreferrer"` is missing on the Telegram link. While `noopener` prevents `window.opener` access, `noreferrer` prevents the Referer header from leaking the page URL. Minor but good practice.

### 19. RTL layout: `direction:ltr` on referral link input may cause UX confusion
**[SEV: minor — P2]**
**File:** `app/templates/account.html:~170`

```html
<div style="display:flex; gap:8px; margin-top:10px; direction:ltr;">
```

**Evidence:** The entire flex container is set to LTR, which reverses the visual order of the input and copy button on an RTL page. The copy button appears on the right (expected position for LTR) but users in RTL context expect it on the left. This is a minor UX inconsistency.

**Fix:** Keep the container RTL and only set `direction:ltr` on the input element itself.

### 21. Admin page: `savePlan` uses `Alpine.store` with duplicate `x-init`
**[SEV: moderate — P2]**
**File:** `app/templates/admin.html:~280-285`

```html
<td><input x-data x-model="$store.plans['{{ p.key }}'].price" 
    x-init="$store.plans['{{ p.key }}'] = {price: {{ p.price_toman }}, active: {{ 'true' if p.active else 'false' }}}" ...>
<td><label><input type="checkbox" x-data x-model="$store.plans['{{ p.key }}'].active" 
    x-init="$store.plans['{{ p.key }}'] = {price: {{ p.price_toman }}, active: {{ 'true' if p.active else 'false' }}}">
```

**Evidence:** The store is initialized twice for each plan (once per input). The second `x-init` overwrites the first, which means if a user changes the price and then the checkbox re-initializes, the price change is lost. Race condition on Alpine initialization order.

**Fix:** Initialize the store once per plan row (on the `<tr>` element) rather than on each input.

### 22. Subscription cancel: two-step confirm uses `$el.dataset` incorrectly with Alpine
**[SEV: moderate — P2]**
**File:** `app/templates/account.html:~130-133`

```html
<button ... x-show="s.active && $el.dataset.confirm !== '1'" @click="cancel(s.id)">لغو</button>
<button ... x-show="s.active && $el.dataset.confirm === '1'" @click="doCancel(s.id)">مطمئنی؟</button>
```

```javascript
async cancel(id) {
  const row = document.querySelector('[data-sub="' + id + '"]');
  if (row) row.dataset.confirm = '1';
}
```

**Evidence:** `$el.dataset.confirm` refers to the button's own dataset, but `cancel()` sets `dataset.confirm` on the parent row (`[data-sub]`). The `x-show` checks `$el.dataset.confirm` (the button itself), which is never set. The two-step confirmation will never work — the "مطمئنی؟" button will never appear.

**Fix:** Use Alpine reactive state instead of DOM dataset:
```javascript
// In subs() data:
confirming: null,
cancel(id) { this.confirming = id; },
doCancel(id) { /* ... */ this.confirming = null; }
// In template:
x-show="s.active && confirming !== s.id"  // for cancel button
x-show="s.active && confirming === s.id"  // for confirm button
```

### 23. `clearSecret` two-step: `btn.dataset.orig` never set
**[SEV: minor — P2]**
**File:** `app/templates/admin.html` (JS `clearSecret` and `regenOrder`)

```javascript
if (!btn.dataset.arm){ 
  btn.dataset.arm = '1'; 
  btn.textContent = 'مطمئنی؟ دوباره بزن'; 
  setTimeout(()=>{ delete btn.dataset.arm; btn.textContent = btn.dataset.orig || btn.textContent; }, 4000); 
  return; 
}
btn.textContent = btn.dataset.orig || btn.textContent;
```

**Evidence:** `btn.dataset.orig` is never set before being read. After the timeout, the button text reverts to whatever `btn.textContent` is at that moment (which is "مطمئنی؟ دوباره بزن"), not the original text. The button label is permanently corrupted after one use.

**Fix:** Save the original text before overwriting:
```javascript
if (!btn.dataset.arm){
  btn.dataset.orig = btn.textContent;  // ← add this
  btn.dataset.arm = '1';
  btn.textContent = 'مطمئنی؟ دوباره بزن';
  ...
```

### 24. `form.html`: year validation allows Gregorian years < 1900 and Jalali years > 1500
**[SEV: minor — P2]**
**File:** `app/templates/form.html:~50`

```html
<input class="input" type="number" x-model.number="year" ... min="1300" max="2100">
```

**Evidence:** The min/max is static regardless of calendar type. For Jalali, 1300-1500 is reasonable (1921-2121 CE). For Gregorian, 1300 is too old (year 1300 CE). No client-side validation differentiates.

**Fix:** Dynamically set min/max based on `cal`:
```javascript
:min="cal === 'jalali' ? 1300 : 1900" :max="cal === 'jalali' ? 1500 : 2100"
```

### 25. `chart.html`: report polling has no timeout/max-retry
**[SEV: moderate — P2]**
**File:** `app/templates/chart.html` (JS `_poll()`)

```javascript
async _poll(){
  while(this.repStatus === 'queued' || this.repStatus === 'running'){
    await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 6000));
    const r = await fetch(...);
    ...
  }
}
```

**Evidence:** If the report generation hangs indefinitely on the server, this polls forever every 6 seconds. On mobile, this drains battery and data. No maximum retry count or timeout.

**Fix:** Add a max iteration count (e.g., 100 iterations = 10 minutes) and show a "taking too long" message:
```javascript
let attempts = 0;
while(...) {
  if (++attempts > 100) { this.repStatus = 'failed'; break; }
  ...
}
```

### 26. `base.html`: third-party analytics script loaded without SRI
**[SEV: moderate — P2]**
**File:** `app/templates/base.html:22`

```html
<script async src="https://analytics.negar.io/script.js" data-website-id="..."></script>
```

**Evidence:** No `integrity` attribute (Subresource Integrity). If `analytics.negar.io` is compromised, arbitrary JS executes on every page of the site. Given this is a SaaS handling payment flows and personal data, this is a meaningful supply-chain risk.

**Fix:** Add SRI hash: `integrity="sha384-..."` and `crossorigin="anonymous"`. Alternatively, self-host the analytics script.

---

### 27. `chat.html`: remaining quota not decremented client-side after send
**[SEV: minor — P2]**
**File:** `app/templates/chat.html` (JS `chat.send()`)

**Evidence:** After a successful message, `this.remaining` is never decremented. The UI shows stale quota until page reload. Users may send more messages than their quota allows (server should enforce, but UX is misleading).

**Fix:** Add `this.remaining = Math.max(0, this.remaining - 1);` after successful send.
